item.title: How 6 were burnt to death, 12 injured in Lagos road accident
item.description: By Esther Onyegbulam, Matthew Johnson & Patrick Chidubem Six persons were burnt to death, while 12 others sustained varying degrees of burns yesterday after a commercial vehicle caught fire at Magbon, along the Lagos-Badagry Expressway. The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, which confirmed the incident, said the victims comprised two females and four males, all adults. It added that the 12 injured persons were rescued and taken to Badagry General Hospital for medical attention. However, an eyewitness account shared in a video gave a different initial account of the tragedy, claiming that many people were feared dead, with only two occupants, reportedly the driver and another passenger, surviving the incident. According to the eyewitness, the accident occurred between 8am and 9am and involved a commercial bus travelling from Mile 2 towards Badagry. The incident reportedly happened shortly after Checking Point Bus Stop, before the Black Signboard axis of the expressway. The eyewitness account indicated that the vehicle caught fire, resulting in multiple casualties. However, the initial casualty figures could not be independently verified. In its official account, the Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, said the agency received a distress call at 8:44am, while firefighters from its Badagry station arrived at the scene at 9:13am. According to Adeseye, “Preliminary information gathered during the investigation indicated that the driver reportedly had an additional five litres of fuel stored inside the vehicle, intending to refuel the vehicle’s tank. The presence of the extra fuel is suspected to have contributed to the intensity of the fire. “Tragically, six persons, comprising two females and four males, all adults, were involved in the incident. item.title: Sexual violence: UK, Mirabel Centre push for stronger protection, Justice for survivors
item.description: *Mrs Sanwo-Olu hails centre’s 10,000-Survivor Care Milestone By Henry Ojelu THE United Kingdom and the Mirabel Centre have called for stronger protection, sustained support and access to justice for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence in Nigeria. The British Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Mr Jonny Baxter, and founder of the Mirabel Centre, Itoro Eze-Anaba, made the call on Thursday at a reception and panel discussion in Lagos to mark the centre’s milestone of supporting more than 10,000 survivors of sexual violence. The event, held as part of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, also featured the launch of the centre’s publication, The Survivor Experience: A Voice That Matters. Speaking on the theme, “A Milestone of Care, A Call for Sustained Support & Justice,” Baxter said the achievement deserved celebration but stressed that sexual violence remained a serious issue requiring sustained attention and commitment. He said: “We want to celebrate 10,000 survivors, but we also want to ensure that many more people are able to access the professional support and services they need.” Baxter emphasised the importance of placing survivors’ experiences at the centre of interventions, saying their voices were essential to understanding their challenges and improving access to support and justice. He reaffirmed the UK’s commitment to ending violence against women and girls through development partnerships and collaboration with governments and civil society organisations. He also disclosed that the UK would soon host an international summit on technology-facilitated gender-based violence, noting that emerging forms of abuse required new approaches and solutions. Earlier, Eze-Anaba acknowledged the contributions of the British Council, the Department for International Development and the British High Commission to the establishment and growth of the centre. She said the British High Commission funded the centre’s first three years and continued to support its work through partnerships and advocacy opportunities. It is about the services we provide and how those services are shared in a dignified manner for survivors,” she said. Eze-Anaba said the centre regularly sought feedback from survivors and had engaged an independent consultant to assess its services, identify gaps and recommend improvements. Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” Anaba also raised concerns over the location of some public schools close to bus stops, motor parks and train stations, warning that such environments could expose children to negative influences at a critical stage of their development. He said children’s welfare must not be treated as an annual talking point without measurable commitments. “It is not enough for us to be episodic. Every year we come and remind ourselves that look, we have to build a future for the kids. Last year, on this same programme, I made a commitment on behalf of my newspaper that Vanguard would do more. Have we done enough?” he asked. He called for an action plan spelling out what government, media organisations, businesses and other stakeholders would do to improve children’s lives. Speaking, UNICEF Representative in Nigeria, Wafaa Saeed, called for sustained investment in children, particularly during the first 1,000 days of life, warning that neglect during this period could have lifelong consequences. “You cannot pause a baby’s brain development while waiting for economic recovery. From conception to age two, 80 percent of human brain growth occurs, making investment in the first 1,000 days critical to a child’s survival, development and future,” Saeed said. She urged journalists to go beyond reporting statistics and highlight the experiences of vulnerable children and families. “Statistics only matter when they move us to protect the child behind the number. We need the media to humanize the numbers, keep children in the headlines year-round and spotlight the solutions that are working across Nigeria,” she said. In her keynote address, Lagos State First Lady, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, said supporting mothers and investing early in children were essential to building a healthier and better-educated generation. She said the Babajide Sanwo-Olu administration remained committed to inclusive child development and gender-responsive governance, ensuring that every child, irrespective of gender, had the opportunity to realise his or her potential. On the proposed review of the Lagos State Child’s Rights Law 2015, she said: “As we undertake the review of the Child’s Rights Law 2015, we have before us a unique opportunity to strengthen our legal and institutional framework in ways that respond to emerging realities while safeguarding the best interests of every child.” Providing further insight into the child health situation, Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Primary Health Care Board, Dr Ibrahim Akinwunmi-Mustafa, said Nigeria had made progress in reducing under-five mortality but continued to face serious challenges in newborn survival and childhood malnutrition. “Under-five deaths have fallen from 132 to 110 per 1,000 live births since 2018. But newborn deaths have barely moved, and four in ten Nigerian children are still stunted.” He disclosed that child stunting in Lagos was about 17 per cent, compared with 40 per cent nationally, while an estimated 120,000 to 130,000 children in the state had never received a single vaccine. “Most of them live in our informal settlements, riverine communities and fast-growing areas,” he said. Mustafa called for stronger primary healthcare financing, investment in frontline health workers and improved access to antenatal care, nutrition counselling, immunisation and birth registration. He also urged journalists to support public health campaigns, counter misinformation and hold government and other stakeholders accountable. “To our friends in the media: you are partners in this work, not spectators,” he said. Also speaking, the Director of Corporate Communications and Corporate Social Responsibility at Airtel Nigeria, Adefemi Adeniran, said a child’s background, economic circumstances or developmental differences should not determine his or her future. “Neither the economic circumstances of a child’s parent, background nor their developmental differences should determine a child’s prospects in life. Keeping them alive is our fundamental obligation. Enabling them to learn is our collective responsibility. Creating conditions for them to thrive must be our shared ambition,” he said. Also the DAME Trustee, Mr. Lanre Idowu, said the partnership between UNICEF, NGE and DAME was helping to strengthen child-rights journalism through training, access to credible evidence, field visits and recognition of excellent reporting. On his part, UNICEF Nigeria Goodwill Ambassador and musician, Cobhams Asuquo, highlighted the role of music in communicating messages about child survival and development. “Music is a powerful tool. It can take an important message beyond the statistics and help people connect with the real lives and experiences behind it. With the First 1,000 Days of Life song, we wanted families and communities to understand that what we do for a child from the very beginning, the nutrition, care and support we provide, can shape that child’s future,” he said. Children also participated in the discussions, questioning decision-makers on how they would ensure that poverty, gender, disability and family circumstances did not deny any child access to healthcare, education and protection. Their performances, including “The First 1,000 Days of Life” and “I Am a Nigerian Child,” reinforced the importance of including children’s voices in decisions affecting their future. The symposium coincided with UNICEF’s 80th anniversary, with participants renewing calls for sustained government leadership, adequate financing, private sector investment, community participation and media accountability to secure a better future for Nigerian children. item.title: Stay away from our state, Imo APC tells Wike
item.description: The All Progressives Congress, APC, in Imo State, has declared that the state is not available for political manipulation or interference by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Nyesom Wike. Read Also: ‘I’m done with Rivers, FCT; give me Imo, Kwara to deliver’ – Wike tells Tinubu It vowed to resist any attempt to import what it described as his controversial political tactics into the state ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party made its position known in a statement yesterday by its State Publicity Secretary, Onwuasoanya Jones in reaction to alleged Wike’s recent claim that he had concluded arrangements to secure electoral victories for President Bola Tinubu and the APC in the forthcoming elections. Wike was also reported to have offered to undertake additional political assignments for the President, including delivering other states for the APC. Reacting, the Imo APC dismissed the minister’s claims, contending that he should not assume that his political activities could determine the electoral fortunes of the party in different states. The statement particularly faulted Wike for reportedly suggesting that Imo State and another APC-controlled state had political problems requiring his intervention. “We would have ignored the politically displaced errand boy, like we always do, but for the fact that we deem this particular statement of his a direct affront on the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the electoral integrity of our dear party, the APC,” the statement declared. The party accused the FCT minister of attempting to portray President Tinubu as politically dependent on individuals outside the APC to secure electoral victories, insisting that the party enjoys its own grassroots support and political structure. It also faulted Wike’s reported assertion that he had already secured victory for the APC in the FCT and Rivers State, describing such declarations, made weeks before the elections, as disrespectful to democratic principles and the electorate. According to the statement, “our party, the All Progressives Congress, has immense regard for the Nigerian people and would not encourage actions and utterances that tend to cast the Nigerian electorate as irrelevant in the determination of their political future.” The Imo APC further accused Wike of taking advantage of the party’s political goodwill to sustain his relevance while allegedly making disparaging remarks about some of its leaders. It challenged the minister to demonstrate his political influence by campaigning for his own party, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), rather than making claims about delivering APC victories. On the political situation in Imo State, the party maintained that its activities were progressing without difficulty and expressed confidence in its preparations for the 2027 elections. It said its mobilisation efforts across the state were ongoing, adding that it expected Imo voters to participate in the forthcoming elections

item.title: Security chiefs hail IGP Disu for suspending declaration of Obaigbena, others wanted
item.description: By Emma Nnadozie THE police order suspending the wanted declaration on Arise TV owner, Mr. Nduka Obaigbena and seven others over alleged assassination attempt by Assistant Inspector-General of Police, Olohundare Jimoh, has elicited reactions from some security chiefs in the country, who said that the wanted declaration was done without due process. One of the security chiefs who spoke with Vanguard, said: “It was misappropriate and procedurally flawed” and showered encomiums on the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, for his quick response by suspending the wanted declaration The Assistant Inspector-General of Police, Zone 2, Onikan, Lagos, Olohundare Jimoh, last Tuesday, declared Chairman of Arise News and This Day Media Group, Chief Nduka Obaigbena, Managing Director of Nestoil, Dr. Ernest Azudialu-Obiejesi, and seven others wanted over an alleged threat to the life of First Bank Managing Director, Olusegun Alebiosu in a crowed press conference in Lagos. He said the declaration followed an investigation into the delivery of a parcel containing two rounds of 7.62mm live ammunition to Alebiosu’s residence in Lagos. However, in a swift reaction two days later, the IGP, through the Force Public Relations Officer, FPRO, Ani Iniedu suspended the wanted declaration against the suspects and stated that the case has been transferred to the Force Intelligence Department, FID, Abuja, for a thorough and impartial investigation. Explaining how perpetrators operate, he said many exploit social media to establish relationships with unsuspecting young men and women, build their confidence and lure them into physical meetings under false pretences. According to him, victims are sometimes encouraged to travel long distances, with perpetrators offering to pay their transport fares, book hotel accommodation or even arrange flights. However, upon arriving at the agreed locations, some victims reportedly discover that the meetings are traps. Their phones and valuables are seized, while others are kidnapped, sexually assaulted, filmed in compromising situations or threatened with the publication of nude pictures. The images are subsequently used to blackmail victims and extort money from them, often leaving them too ashamed or traumatised to report the incidents to their families or law enforcement agencies. The representative said some victims resorted to stealing and other desperate measures to meet the demands of their blackmailers, while others suffered severe psychological trauma. He also raised concerns over mob attacks and killings arising from rumours and allegations circulated online, warning that innocent people had been attacked or killed without investigations. “We have seen mob violence. We have seen several persons have been killed, some of them innocently. People who are not supposed to be killed are killed,” he said. He urged communities to reject jungle justice and allow law enforcement agencies to investigate allegations and ensure that anyone found culpable was prosecuted in accordance with the law. “Instead of taking laws in your hand, you report to the leaders of the community. The leaders do a follow-up, do their investigation, also using the state machinery, then those that need to be truly punished, let them be punished according to the law of the land, not on the basis of what a group of persons decide at any point.” The organisation also called for the protection of victims’ identities, warning that public exposure, rumour-mongering and stigmatisation could deepen their trauma and discourage others from reporting abuse. On available support, the representative said Lagos State had six sexual assault referral centres where survivors could receive treatment free of charge. He identified the Lagos State Domestic and Sexual Violence Response Agency, the Office of the Public Defender and the National Human Rights Commission as other institutions victims could approach for assistance, including legal support. He said ISHRAI would provide the necessary linkages to ensure that victims were referred to appropriate services. Lawal disclosed that the next step would be to establish a referral pathway through a WhatsApp platform involving the participating community leaders, alongside a directory of relevant government agencies and support organisations. She said the initiative would also encourage the leaders to take the message back to their communities and commit themselves to preventing human rights violations. Also speaking, a Health Education Officer with the Lagos State Primary Health Care Board, Lagos State Health District 6, Mrs Rashida Sanni’Afolabi, described the engagement as an important opportunity to strengthen community participation in protecting vulnerable people. She said traditional rulers, religious leaders and ward health committee members were strategically positioned to bridge the gap between communities and the healthcare system because of their closeness to the people. Sanni’Afolabi stressed that victims of sexual violence should not be blamed or subjected to judgment when they seek help. “Take for instance, someone that’s been raped, a lady that’s been raped, we should not start with the question of why were you raped, probably because she didn’t dress well, but we should remember that we need to address the issue first, so that people can feel safer, they will be able to come out and tell us how they feel,” she said. She urged health workers and community stakeholders to incorporate awareness of rights, sexual and gender-based violence and available support services into their engagements, including school health programmes. According to her, addressing such violence requires a holistic approach that considers the physical, mental and emotional wellbeing of affected persons. The stakeholders agreed that closer collaboration among traditional institutions, religious organisations, government agencies and civil society groups would be necessary to strengthen reporting, protect survivors and ensure that allegations of criminal conduct were handled through lawful channels. ISHRAI said it would continue to support community leaders with information and referral services, stressing that public awareness, respect for human dignity and rejection of violence were essential to preventing further victimisation. item.title: ‘Sanitation exercise to hold Saturday as scheduled’ – Lagos Govt
item.description: The Lagos State Government has dismissed rumours of a postponement of the November monthly environmental sanitation exercise, confirming that it will hold across the state on Saturday, November 28, 2026. The exercise is scheduled to take place between 6:30am and 8:30am and will be monitored by government officials across various local government areas and local council development areas. The state government made the clarification on Thursday in a statement signed by Kunle Adeshina, Director of Public Affairs, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources. The statement quoted the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen, as saying there was no basis for postponing the exercise. “There is no basis to cancel the monthly exercise which has become a rallying point for everyone to stay back and clean their neighbourhood,” Tajudeen said. He added that the November edition would be monitored across the state, as had become a tradition. According to the statement, the First Lady of Lagos State, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, will lead a team of government officials to monitor the exercise in Eti-Osa Local Government Area. Similarly, another team led by the Head of Service, Mr Olabode Agoro, will monitor activities in Coker-Aguda Local Council Development Area. Explaining the timing of the exercise, Tajudeen said the 6:30am to 8:30am schedule would allow residents to participate in the clean-up without disrupting other activities. He said the timeframe “gives enough room for any form of civic exercise to still be undertaken after the clean-up.” The permanent secretary urged Lagos residents to remain in their neighbourhoods and participate actively in the exercise. He also called on transport unions to use the opportunity to clean their parks and garages before resuming passenger operations at 8:30am. The state government reiterated its call for collective participation in maintaining environmental cleanliness across Lagos State. item.title: 2027: Ebonyi CP warns parties against electoral violence
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Commissioner of Police, Hope Urunwa Okafor, has warned political parties and their leaders against violence, thuggery and hate speech ahead of the 2027 general elections. Okafor gave the warning during a meeting she convened with leaders and representatives of political parties in the state to discuss strategies for ensuring peaceful political activities ahead of the elections. The meeting was attended by representatives of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), National Democratic Congress (NDC), All Progressives Congress (APC), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and Because Of Our Tomorrow (BOOT) Party. The police commissioner reiterated that the Nigeria Police Force remained apolitical and impartial in the discharge of its duties. She assured the party leaders that the command was prepared to provide adequate security for campaign activities, protect lives and property, and maintain law and order across the state. Okafor stressed that no society could thrive in an atmosphere of violence, urging political parties to avoid inflammatory rhetoric, hate speech, personal attacks and other forms of communication capable of inciting violence. She charged party leaders to demonstrate responsible leadership by ensuring that their words and actions promoted peaceful political engagement. The commissioner also urged them to demonstrate zero tolerance for violence among their supporters, rather than merely preaching peace. She called on the political parties to exercise restraint in their public statements and campaign activities and provide the command with timely information on their campaign schedules and other political engagements to enable adequate security arrangements. In their separate remarks, the party representatives commended the commissioner for convening the meeting, describing it as timely and necessary ahead of the 2027 elections. They appealed to the police command to provide adequate security during campaigns and other political activities. The party representatives also requested that candidates contesting various elective positions be invited to similar engagements to strengthen collective efforts towards peaceful elections. item.title: Fountain of Life Church challenges bench warrant against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya
item.description: The Fountain of Life Church has raised concerns over the issuance of a bench warrant against its Senior Pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, by the Lagos State High Court, questioning the procedure leading to the order. In a statement dated November 26, 2026, the church said the development followed proceedings before Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin, which also culminated in the judge’s recusal from the case. The church claimed that Odukoya had not been formally served with the restraining order, originating processes and accompanying documents, either personally or through substituted service, as directed by the court. It also alleged that directives contained in the court’s orders of November 18 and 23 concerning the service of the documents remained unfulfilled. According to the church, its legal representatives had already filed a Notice of Appeal and two separate motions challenging the orders, their enforcement, the court’s jurisdiction and the contempt proceedings. The church further claimed that the matter was not listed on the court’s cause list for November 26 and that members of the media were asked to leave the courtroom before the bench warrant was issued. It said the warrant was issued without the court first determining the pending applications, after which the presiding judge recused herself. “These developments occurred within eight days of the initial ex parte order and before 1 December 2026, the date originally fixed by the court for mention,” the statement said. The church described the circumstances as raising serious questions about due process, fair hearing and the administration of justice. It added that its lawyers were challenging the orders and related procedural and jurisdictional issues before the appropriate courts, including the Court of Appeal. Clarifying the implications of the warrant, the church said its issuance did not amount to a conviction or a final determination of the substantive leadership dispute. The church also maintained that Odukoya remained its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, describing the position as part of the issues being pursued through the judicial process. It urged members and the general public to remain calm, united and prayerful, adding that it would exhaust all available legal remedies within the Nigerian judicial system. Tevez started his career at Boca Juniors and returned there in 2018 before retiring four years later, and now his testimonial will be played December 20 at their Bombonera stadium in Buenos Aires. Messi, 39, and 41-year-old Ronaldo have faced off against each other many times on the pitch, notably in several El Clasico fixtures during their respective times at Barcelona and Real Madrid. item.description: Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan, who had lost three of their opening four matches, gave their hopes of avoiding an embarrassing early exit a boost with a 4-2 victory at Olympiakos. Hutchinson added another assist as he crossed for Christian Pulisic to volley home 19 minutes from time, before Diego Moreira’s injury-time fourth, breathing life into the seven-time European champions’ campaign. item.title: Gbajabiamila leads Tinubu’s delegation to IBB, Abdulsalami
item.description: Chief of Staff to President Bola Tinubu, Femi Gbajabiamila, on Thursday led a presidential delegation to Minna, Niger State, to pay courtesy visits to former military Heads of State, Generals Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida and Abdulsalami Abubakar. Gbajabiamila disclosed this in a statement, saying the visit was undertaken at the directive of President Tinubu to convey his goodwill and best wishes to the two elder statesmen. He said the delegation was warmly received by both former leaders, who appeared well and in high spirits during the visits. According to him, Babangida expressed satisfaction with the Tinubu administration’s performance, reaffirmed his support for the President and wished him success. Abdulsalami, on his part, commended the administration’s performance and thanked Tinubu for remembering the former leaders despite the demands of the ongoing election campaign. Gbajabiamila described the two former leaders as important figures in Nigeria’s history, noting that their experience and counsel remained invaluable to the country. “These are men who occupy major chapters in Nigeria’s history and their counsel remains invaluable,” he said. He added that the President was pleased with their support and expressed optimism about their continued backing in the coming elections. The visits come amid heightened political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, as political parties and their candidates intensify consultations and mobilise support across the country. Babangida, who ruled Nigeria from 1985 to 1993, remains one of the country’s most influential former military leaders, while Abdulsalami, who assumed power in June 1998, oversaw the transition programme that ushered in the Fourth Republic in May 1999.

item.title: Mock Accreditation: INEC Faces Crucial Test As 100 Million Voters Await 2027 Elections
item.description: With exactly 50 days before Nigerians return to the ballot, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is preparing for a nationwide test that could offer an important indication of whether the country is ready for another fiercely contested general election. On Saturday, November 28, the electoral umpire will deploy its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and electronic results upload technology across 17,676 selected polling units in a mock exercise designed to identify operational weaknesses, test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. The exercise, scheduled for 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., will cover two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas, giving INEC an opportunity to assess the performance of its electoral technology across different locations before the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, and the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6. #OsunDecides2026: Election Officers Take Delivery Of Materials, Mobilise To Polling Units during the Osun State governorship election on August 15, 2026. It comes against the backdrop of lingering controversies surrounding the 2023 general elections, particularly the failure to upload presidential election results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) in real time, technical difficulties associated with BVAS and allegations of electoral irregularities. Chairman of INEC, Joash Amupitan, described the mock exercise as an important part of preparations for the forthcoming elections, while urging Nigerians to participate. The commission’s Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria Meci, explained that the exercise would allow INEC to establish the effectiveness and reliability of its equipment before election day. “We don’t want to wait till the elections before we test the ruggedness, readiness and functionality of the system,” she said during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . According to her, the commission has reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS device, with additional machines to be provided at polling units with larger voter populations. The exercise will also test the electronic upload of results to IReV, although Meci acknowledged that successful transmission would depend on network availability. 100 Million Voters, 176,846 Polling Units The scale of the preparations reflects the size of Nigeria’s electorate. INEC says it is now managing a verified national register of more than 100 million voters after removing over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated, and deceased records from the previous register of approximately 103 million. Amupitan disclosed on Wednesday, during a meeting with resident electoral commissioners from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, that the clean-up followed the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System and a statutory claims-and-objections audit. According to her, the commission has reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS device, with additional machines to be provided at polling units with larger voter populations. The exercise will also test the electronic upload of results to IReV, although Meci acknowledged that successful transmission would depend on network availability. 100 Million Voters, 176,846 Polling Units The scale of the preparations reflects the size of Nigeria’s electorate. INEC says it is now managing a verified national register of more than 100 million voters after removing over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated, and deceased records from the previous register of approximately 103 million. Amupitan disclosed on Wednesday, during a meeting with resident electoral commissioners from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, that the clean-up followed the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System and a statutory claims-and-objections audit. Photo: Taiwo Adesina/Channels TV He said the three phases of Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) conducted since 2025 attracted more than 11 million registrations, with over 10.77 million new registrants retained. The commission also received approximately 311,000 complaints during the claims-and-objections exercise, of which about 232,000 were found to be genuine and addressed. “By the time we are putting the verified and cleaned-up register together, the national voters’ register is reduced from 103 million to 100 million,” Amupitan said. The chairman added that 232,658 persons with disabilities were captured in the register, requiring accessible polling arrangements and appropriate assistive materials. Before the latest clean-up, Lagos had the highest number of registered voters, with 7,488,633, followed by Kano with 6,570,276 and Kaduna with 4,662,640. Other states among the top 10 were Katsina (3,876,051), Rivers (3,736,434), Oyo (3,588,111), Delta (3,525,988), Benue (3,057,225), Ogun (3,037,981) and Bauchi (3,012,547). Nigeria currently has 176,846 polling units across 8,809 wards, with electoral activities expected to involve more than 1.41 million ad hoc personnel. INEC also says it has deployed 57,000 newly procured BVAS devices nationwide. 2023 Controversies, 2027 Confidence Questions However, the commission’s preparations are unfolding amid concerns about the credibility of the electoral process. The 2023 presidential election, which produced four major contenders, remains an important reference point for the coming contest. ﻿ President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC) secured 8,794,726 votes to defeat former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, then of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), who polled 6,984,520. Peter Obi, who was of the Labour Party, finished third with 6,101,533 votes, while Rabiu Kwankwaso, then of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP), secured 1,496,687 votes. The four politicians remain prominent figures in the political calculations surrounding 2027. Beyond the political contest, the credibility of INEC’s technology and the transparency of its operations remain major concerns. A former resident electoral commissioner, Mike Igini, argued that the failure to transmit results from the 2023 presidential election eroded public confidence in the commission. He said that despite serving as a REC, he could not clearly explain the technical glitch INEC attributed to the failure, insisting that the experience undermined trust in the electoral umpire. “Now, in 2023, what worked and what broke public confidence? The BVAS worked. But what broke confidence, which has created a liability and a cloud of distrust that the current leadership is suffering, was the fact that there were three elections, same day; only one could not be transmitted, which was the presidential,” Igini said on Channels Television’s Politics Today . “That was what evaporated public trust and confidence. Even people like us, who put out our integrity to explain to people, to give a clarion call to the Nigerian people, up till date I don’t have a clear explanation of what constituted that glitch.” A September 2026 survey by Yiaga Africa also highlighted the challenge. Its findings showed that only 34 per cent of respondents were confident that INEC would conduct credible elections, down from 45 per cent in previous surveys. Although 84 per cent indicated that they were likely or very likely to vote, 61 per cent said fear of electoral violence could discourage them from participating. The survey also found that 49 per cent trusted BVAS and IReV, highlighting the need for greater transparency in the deployment of electoral technology. Logistics, Security Beyond technology, INEC’s ability to recruit and deploy sufficient personnel presents another challenge. The commission recently disclosed that political violence was discouraging prospective ad hoc staff, particularly members of the National Youth Service Corps, from applying for election duties. This photo shows ad hoc staff of INEC awaiting mobilisation for the 2026 Osun governorship election on August 15, 2026. Its Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria Eta-Mesi, said the commission had not received the number of applications required to commence training, prompting a two-week extension of the recruitment deadline to December 3, 2026. “We didn’t have the numbers that we require to train for the election,” she said. INEC has identified insecurity, logistics and results management as major priorities, while acknowledging that the commission is still awaiting the outstanding portion of its 2027 election budget.
